title: DataAccessV1dot24
description: K-05 v1.24, a minor version of the data-access calls (T-1549: the ruling T-1543's card A9, ops/reviews/signup-remainder/rule-rest.json; DL-1194): the runtime-side reads the rest of journey 1's sign-up by text needs, and the text way of a sign-in. It only adds to v1.23 (data-access.v1.23.schema.json, frozen and unchanged, referred to here, which refers on to every earlier version down to v1): every v1.23 definition is here under its own name, by reference, and none changes but the three it restates, startSignIn.request (v1.13's form, or v1.24's startSignIn.textRequest), startSignIn.response (v1.13's started or paused, or v1.24's startSignIn.textStarted) and startSignIn.exchange (to refer to v1.24's request and response; the errors v1.14's, by reference), so every v1 to v1.23 exchange is a v1.24 exchange. Added, each on the runtime side as rosie_job in a read-only transaction of its own, 1 connection, never on or beside a Tool API call's transaction (README items 85 to 92): readSignUpKeys (S1-10's keys by person: README item 85), readPendingUpload (the pending upload by its upload id: item 86), openReviewItemsOf (a business's open K-37 review items of one kind, never the summary: item 88), readStagingTestBusinesses (the businesses whose owner's account mobile is one of the numbers given: item 89), startSignIn.textRequest, startSignIn.textStarted and startSignIn.textExchange (the text way of a sign-in's start: item 90), and liveTextSignInCode (the id of a handle's live sign-in code that went by text, never its hash: item 91). Item 87 (item 26 reads the K-23 v1.1 claim as facts) and item 92 (a handle's phone service) add no call. No column, grant, index or migration is added. Not model-facing, so number and length limits are schema rules here. Owner: the architect.

startSignIn.textRequest.title: StartSignInTextRequest
startSignIn.textRequest.description: A sign-in's start by the text way, before the page answers (README item 90; R29; MC C9; K-21 v1 signInStart's way text and fixture sign-in-from-link-by-text; K-22 v1.2 sign_in_attempts.way, which admits text). v1.13's request (startSignIn.request: the same ids, hashes, key name and no time) with way text, a mobile contact alone, and the code the page's ready text will carry, as its keyed hash and the id of its K-22 proof_codes row: the page call makes the code (6 digits from a cryptographically secure generator, as for email) and puts it only in its own answer's ready text, never in this request, a span or a log. Role and scope: v1.13's (rosie_job on the runtime side through HYPERDRIVE_JOB, ADR-016 section 6; rosie.business_id set empty, rosie.person_id unset), its own transaction, 1 connection, never in one transaction with a Tool API call. Rules 0 to 5 run as for email (README item 58), the account found by its mobile; with exactly one account the same transaction writes the code row, channel text, to that mobile's handle (README item 90, default 229). Repeat: safe, keyed by requestSha256: a repeat answers the first attempt and writes nothing. New in v1.24.

contact.description: The account's own mobile as typed and normalized (E.164): the text way signs in only from the account's own mobile (R29; MC C9), so an email or a link names no phone the ready text could come from (refuse-start-sign-in-text-email-contact).

way.description: text: the owner proves the attempt by texting the page's ready text from the account's own mobile to Rosie's number, where the turn carrying it checks the code (K-21 README lines 112 and 120; R29). No code is texted to anyone.

codeId.description: K-22 proof_codes.id for the code row this start writes when it finds exactly one account (README item 90): made by the page call from at least 128 bits of a cryptographically secure generator, never from the attempt, the contact or the time. Dropped, with nothing written, on a repeat, a pause, or no account or two. It is the id liveTextSignInCode later answers (README item 91), never the code.

codeHash.description: K-22 proof_codes.code_hash: HMAC-SHA-256 of the code under hashKeyName's secret, in lower-case hex (K-22 proof_codes_hash_form), made as for an email code (sendSignInCode.request), so K-22 check_proof_code checks the code the text carries against it alone. Never the code (BP rule 7; refuse-start-sign-in-text-plain-code).

startSignIn.request.title: StartSignInRequest
startSignIn.request.description: A sign-in's start (README items 58 and 90): v1.13's form (way email, unchanged) or v1.24's (startSignIn.textRequest: way text, a mobile contact, the code's id and keyed hash). The two never overlap: their way differs. Changed in v1.24.

startSignIn.textStarted.title: StartSignInTextStarted
startSignIn.textStarted.description: Started by the text way (README item 90): v1.13's started answer (the attempt's id, attemptId, expiresAt, repeated and personId, each as v1.13 states it) with codeId, the K-22 proof_codes row this start wrote, for the server only, never the page or a span. personId and codeId are given together: exactly one account whose mobile is the contact, on a start that is not a repeat; both null with no account, two or more, and on every repeat (refuse-start-sign-in-text-repeat-names-code). The page gets attemptId, expiresAt and its own ready text, the same with or without an account; the page call answers its ready text only on a start that is not repeated, so the ready text is answered once (default 230). New in v1.24.

codeId.description: The proof_codes row this start wrote (the request's codeId): purpose sign_in, channel text, sent_to_handle_id the account mobile's handle (phones.handle_id), person_id the account's person, business_id null, sent_at and expires_at by the database's clock, 10 minutes apart. null whenever personId is null.

startSignIn.response.title: StartSignInResponse
startSignIn.response.description: Started or paused (README items 58 and 90): v1.13's started or paused, or v1.24's startSignIn.textStarted, which alone names codeId, so the three never overlap. Changed in v1.24.

startSignIn.exchange.title: StartSignInExchange
startSignIn.exchange.description: One startSignIn request with its outcome, restated in v1.24 to refer to v1.24's request and response; call and given are v1.13's and the errors v1.14's, each by reference. So a request in v1.13's form is a v1.23 exchange. Changed in v1.24.

startSignIn.textExchange.title: StartSignInTextExchange
startSignIn.textExchange.description: The exchange of a start by the text way: startSignIn.exchange narrowed by allOf to startSignIn.textRequest, answered textStarted, paused or an error. The v1.24 sign-in fixtures are listed under this definition, so the loops that select startSignIn.exchange (db/repo/sign-in-send.int.test.ts and the database side) never meet them before db/repo's text way (card A17) merges; it is the definition A17's answers and A15's requests are checked against. New in v1.24.

signUpIdUpload.title: SignUpIdUpload
signUpIdUpload.description: A person's sign_up K-22 id_uploads row as readSignUpKeys gives it (README item 85): its id and uploaded_at alone, the ID half of S1-10's keys (id_checked: K-22 'a sign_up upload counts as the ID confirmed'). Never object_key, which stays sealed in the row and is seen only on the secure page (K-22 id_uploads.object_key, audience secure-page-only; refuse-sign-up-keys-object-key), and never content_type or purpose (always sign_up here). New in v1.24.

signUpMobile.title: SignUpMobile
signUpMobile.description: A person's proven account mobile as readSignUpKeys gives it (README item 85): K-22 accounts.mobile with accounts.mobile_proven_at, and that mobile's K-04 handle id (phones.handle_id, migration 0004 line 41, not null), which K-05 v1.10 item 50 readHandle takes, so the actor that holds the owner's texts is named from it (the runtime engineer's round-3 note 1). Given only when both mobile and mobile_proven_at are set (default 227). New in v1.24.

readSignUpKeys.request.title: ReadSignUpKeysRequest
readSignUpKeys.request.description: S1-10's keys by person (README item 85; K-09 open gap 201; card A9 item 1): the person whose sign-up the event turn walks on from S1-10 for (the link's own person). Role and scope: rosie_job on the runtime side, with no business scope (accounts, id_uploads and phones are scoped none: K-22, K-04), a read-only transaction of its own on the primary, 1 connection, never on or beside a Tool API call's transaction. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources. New in v1.24.

readSignUpKeys.response.title: ReadSignUpKeysResponse
readSignUpKeys.response.description: The person's S1-10 keys, from one read-only transaction (README item 85): idUpload, the person's one sign_up upload (K-22 id_uploads_one_sign_up), or null with none; mobile, the account's proven mobile with its handle id, or null when the person has no account, no mobile or a mobile not proven. A person with no row anywhere answers both null, never an error, so the read never tells whether a person exists. New in v1.24.

readSignUpKeys.errors.title: ReadSignUpKeysErrors
readSignUpKeys.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again. New in v1.24.

readSignUpKeys.exchange.title: ReadSignUpKeysExchange
readSignUpKeys.exchange.description: One readSignUpKeys request with its outcome. New in v1.24.

pendingUpload.title: PendingUpload
pendingUpload.description: An upload signedUpload made and finishUpload checked, by its upload id, as the server keeps it beside the id (K-21 README: 'an upload id the server binds to its key, person, business and purpose'; K-13 README: 'the caller keeps the first with its upload id'): its person, the business its page was for (null for a sign_up ID, which is the person's for every company), its purpose, its media type and its object key sealed under the person's key, the bytes as stored (sealedBytes), never opened on the way. Where the binding is kept is not in a frozen table list (README open gap 107). New in v1.24.

personId.description: The person the upload was made for (the page's signed-in person).

businessId.description: The business the page was for, or null.

purpose.description: K-22 id_uploads.purpose: sign_up (S1-10) or re_check (S13-45 row 8).

contentType.description: The media type checkUpload read from the file's leading bytes (K-13), as K-22 id_uploads_content_type_form takes it.

objectKey.description: The R2 object key, sealed under the person's key (K-22 id_uploads.object_key, sealedBy person_id), never in plain words (refuse-pending-upload-plain-object-key). The event turn copies these bytes into its id_uploads insert as they are.

readPendingUpload.request.title: ReadPendingUploadRequest
readPendingUpload.request.description: The pending upload by its upload id (README item 86; card A9 item 2), read by the event turn's gate (card A11, bound by B11) before it writes S1-10's id_uploads row. Role and scope: rosie_job on the runtime side, with no business scope, a read-only transaction of its own on the primary, 1 connection, never on or beside a Tool API call's transaction. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: inside the event turn's gate (arch 04 line 223). New in v1.24.

uploadId.description: The event's ref (K-21 v1.4 finishUpload's event {key id_checked, step S1-10, ref the upload id}).

readPendingUpload.found.title: ReadPendingUploadFound
readPendingUpload.found.description: The upload, as kept (README item 86). New in v1.24.

readPendingUpload.none.title: ReadPendingUploadNone
readPendingUpload.none.description: No upload is kept under the id, or its file never came (one answer for both, as K-21 v1's uploadNotFound): the event is refused and nothing is written. New in v1.24.

readPendingUpload.response.title: ReadPendingUploadResponse
readPendingUpload.response.description: Found or none (README item 86). New in v1.24.

readPendingUpload.errors.title: ReadPendingUploadErrors
readPendingUpload.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again. New in v1.24.

readPendingUpload.exchange.title: ReadPendingUploadExchange
readPendingUpload.exchange.description: One readPendingUpload request with its outcome. New in v1.24.

reviewItemKind.title: ReviewItemKind
reviewItemKind.description: K-37 v1 review_items.kind (platform-review README; S1-03, S1-75, S1-76, S11-52, S12-28, A3-49, S11-70). New in v1.24.

openReviewItem.title: OpenReviewItem
openReviewItem.description: One open K-37 review item as openReviewItemsOf gives it (README item 88): its id, kind, state (open or waiting: default 228), version and raised_by_person_id, the plain columns a check and a decision at the version read need. Never summary, subject_table, subject_row_id, turn_id, due_at, wait_until or decided_at (refuse-open-review-items-summary): the summary is Rosie's team's words for the team, read only on the team console (K-37 rule 2). New in v1.24.

raisedByPersonId.description: K-37 review_items.raised_by_person_id, or null when Rosie raised it.

openReviewItemsOf.request.title: OpenReviewItemsOfRequest
openReviewItemsOf.request.description: A business's open review items of one kind (README item 88; card A9 item 4): S1-75's check of an open listing_match item (card B8), and staging's review list (card E10). Role and scope: rosie_job on the runtime side (K-37 rule 2: no Tool API role reads review_items; actions/src/domain/paging/ports.ts line 178), with no business scope, every statement naming the request's business, a read-only transaction of its own on the primary beside the call's and never on it, 1 connection. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: inside the gate (arch 04 line 223) for B8; none in the sources for E10. New in v1.24.

openReviewItemsOf.response.title: OpenReviewItemsOfResponse
openReviewItemsOf.response.description: Every review item of the business and kind whose state is not done, in id order; none is an empty list (README item 88). New in v1.24.

openReviewItemsOf.errors.title: OpenReviewItemsOfErrors
openReviewItemsOf.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again. New in v1.24.

openReviewItemsOf.exchange.title: OpenReviewItemsOfExchange
openReviewItemsOf.exchange.description: One openReviewItemsOf request with its outcome. New in v1.24.

readStagingTestBusinesses.request.title: ReadStagingTestBusinessesRequest
readStagingTestBusinesses.request.description: Staging's test businesses (README item 89; card A9 item 5; K-21 v1.4 testReviewItems, card E10): the numbers given are the ones staging lets Rosie text, STAGING_LINQ_ALLOWLIST and the roster's test phones, read by name at run time and never committed, printed or logged. Role and scope: rosie_job on the runtime side, unscoped (person_roles, accounts and businesses read across businesses), a read-only transaction of its own on the primary, 1 connection. Served on staging alone: production's binding never calls it. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: none in the sources. New in v1.24.

numbers.description: The allowed numbers, each in E.164, each once, at least one: an empty list names no test business (refuse-staging-test-businesses-no-numbers).

readStagingTestBusinesses.response.title: ReadStagingTestBusinessesResponse
readStagingTestBusinesses.response.description: The ids of the businesses whose live owner role (K-04 person_roles, role owner, ended_at null) is held by a person whose K-22 account mobile is one of the numbers, in id order, each once; none is an empty list (README item 89, default 232). Ids alone: no number, person, name or role is answered. New in v1.24.

readStagingTestBusinesses.errors.title: ReadStagingTestBusinessesErrors
readStagingTestBusinesses.errors.description: transient alone: the same request may be sent again. New in v1.24.

readStagingTestBusinesses.exchange.title: ReadStagingTestBusinessesExchange
readStagingTestBusinesses.exchange.description: One readStagingTestBusinesses request with its outcome. New in v1.24.

liveTextSignInCode.request.title: LiveTextSignInCodeRequest
liveTextSignInCode.request.description: The live text sign-in code of a handle (README item 91; card A9 item 6; R29), read by the turn's guard when a text of the ready text's exact shape comes from the turn's own handle, before the gate and never in its slot. Role and scope: rosie_job on the runtime side through HYPERDRIVE_JOB (ADR-016 section 6), with no business scope (proof_codes' runtime side), a read-only transaction of its own on the primary, 1 connection, never in one transaction with a Tool API call. Repeat: safe, a read. Time budget: inside the turn's reads, before the gate. New in v1.24.

handleId.description: The turn's own handle (K-04 handles.id), the one the ready text came from.

liveTextSignInCode.live.title: LiveTextSignInCodeLive
liveTextSignInCode.live.description: The id of the handle's live sign-in code that went by text (README item 91, default 231): a K-22 proof_codes row of purpose sign_in, channel text, sent_to_handle_id the handle, used_at null and expires_at after the database's now, the newest by sent_at then id. Its id alone, never its hash, its person or its tries (refuse-live-text-sign-in-code-hash): the code is checked only by K-22 check_proof_code inside K-09 proveCode, its tries counted (RULES 6.2). New in v1.24.

liveTextSignInCode.none.title: LiveTextSignInCodeNone
liveTextSignInCode.none.description: No live text code for the handle: none was written, it was used, or it expired, one answer for each, from the same statement (README item 91). The text then goes on as any text does (R29). New in v1.24.

liveTextSignInCode.response.title: LiveTextSignInCodeResponse
liveTextSignInCode.response.description: Live or none (README item 91). New in v1.24.

liveTextSignInCode.errors.title: LiveTextSignInCodeErrors
liveTextSignInCode.errors.description: transient alone: the run fails as any read of the turn's steps 1 to 6 does, and the lease reruns the turn from its sealed texts; the text is never dropped or sent to decide unread (R29; card A16). New in v1.24.

liveTextSignInCode.exchange.title: LiveTextSignInCodeExchange
liveTextSignInCode.exchange.description: One liveTextSignInCode request with its outcome. New in v1.24.
